body.statement: For every \((n,G,\Sigma,e)\in\mathcal M_1\), \(\mathsf A_1\) runs in time polynomial in the bit length of \((G,\Sigma,e)\) and returns exactly one of: \(\mathrm{(i)}\) the unique value in \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)\), which is rational; \(\mathrm{(ii)}\) two componentwise-quadratic feasible coefficient matrices whose \(e\)-coordinates differ; or \(\mathrm{(iii)}\) a componentwise-quadratic rational description of a feasible curve on which the \(e\)-coordinate is nonconstant. Moreover, \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)\) is respectively a singleton, a two-element set, or a cofinite subset of \(\mathbb R\), and every output has polynomial bit length in the componentwise encoding \(\mathsf{Cert}\). On the fan-in-one class this strictly improves the published polynomial-space numerical edge-identification upper bound of Dörfler et al. to deterministic polynomial bit complexity.
body.justification: The theorem gives a deterministic constructive answer to numerical identification exactly below the proposed fan-in boundary.
body.gap: Dörfler et al. provide only a polynomial-space numerical test in unrestricted graphs, while Gupta and Bläser and Briefs and Bläser solve generic identification on directed trees; this theorem strictly tightens the numerical upper bound on the fan-in-one class and covers every exceptional covariance.
body.consumer: After a latent-to-observed transformation yields maximum indegree one, MIIVsem users can distinguish a failed instrument denominator from genuine nonidentification and receive explicit observationally equivalent coefficient witnesses.
